name: Mutton chops

card.summary: A facial-hair style of long sideburns, sometimes joined by a moustache, that frames the jaw and cheeks and gives the lower face a broader, more defined outline.

quick.overview:
Mutton chops are sideburns grown long and wide down the cheeks, usually with the chin shaved. 'Friendly' mutton chops join the sideburns with a moustache. The style is associated with the Victorian era, and with figures such as Civil War general Ambrose Burnside, from whom the word 'sideburns' derives.

For looks, the style frames the face and adds visual width along the jaw and cheeks. Users with a thinner jaw or a patchy chin sometimes choose it because it works with growth on the sides alone.
quick.how: People grow side whiskers down the face and keep the chin and neck shaved or trimmed, then maintain the outline with a trimmer or razor. Moustache joining and width are style choices.
quick.risks: Skin irritation or ingrown hairs from shaving around the edges can occur. The style reads as retro, rock or rebellious in some settings, which may or may not be the effect wanted.

lead: Mutton chops are a facial-hair style in which sideburns run long and full along the cheeks. 'Friendly mutton chops' connect the sideburns to a moustache while leaving the chin clean-shaven [1].

The name 'sideburns' is said to come from 'burnsides', after Ambrose Burnside, a Civil War general who wore thick sideburns joined to a moustache. Nineteenth-century versions were often more extravagant than modern ones, and Elvis Presley helped spur a 1950s revival among rockers and greasers. They became common across many groups in the 1970s [1].

In appearance terms the style frames the face, widens the lower face visually and adds a distinctive outline. Wikipedia notes it can read as old-fashioned, rough, rebellious or retro [1]. No research on the style's effect on perceived attractiveness was identified.

angle.text: The hair itself creates the outline: width along the jaw and cheeks, with or without a joined moustache. People pick it as a distinctive alternative to a full beard.

paras: Mutton chops leave the chin shaved and grow the sideburns long, often to the jawline or beyond; when joined with a moustache they are called friendly mutton chops [1].

Sideburns are named after Ambrose Burnside. Victorian-era styles hung well below the jaw, a mid-1950s revival followed Elvis Presley, and the 1970s made them widespread. 'Lambchop' sideburns were a symbol in some gay club scenes in San Francisco and Sydney, and musicians such as Neil Young and Lemmy are associated with them [1].

timeline.event: Ambrose Burnside's whiskers give sideburns their name [1].
Revival among rockers and greasers following Elvis Presley [1].
Sideburns become common across many groups [1].
